newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAP rises on repeat of Axa merger talk.
newsitem.headline: UAP rises on repeat of Axa merger talk.

text.p: Shares in French insurer Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) rose on Monday on the back of market rumours of a takeover by Axa, which were denied by UAP, traders said.
"UAP is up on a possible merger with Axa, set off again by a brief article in the Nouvel Observateur," a trader said. The weekly magazine appeared last Thursday but Friday was a public holiday.
UAP stock was up 2.5 francs at 108.70 at 1529 GMT. It rose last Wednesday and Thursday but has fallen 15 percent since the beginning of the year.

The article said UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann was "seduced" by the idea of a merger with Axa, but he had to take into account the management's reluctance. The idea sparked resistance from main shareholder Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) which would have to take a capital loss.
A UAP spokesman once again denied on Monday any negotiations were taking place on an acquisition.
UAP shares have for several weeks have seen buying at around 100 francs and sell orders as it neared 110 francs, traders said.
Friedmann said at the presentation of the firm's half-year results, "I deny all negotiations with whomsoever."
Axa chairman Claude Bebear also denied on September 25 that any talks had been held with UAP on a merger.
